reason: util.parseArgs throws on an unknown flag or a flag without its value and has no non-throwing form. The catch prints the message followed by the usage text on stderr and exits 2. Logging and rethrowing would send the error to Node's uncaught-error report (a stack trace, exit 1) because this call runs before the top-level try, and moving the call inside it would print the message there a second time without the usage text.

readdirSync throws ENOENT for a folder that does not exist yet, which is the normal case of a new --out folder, and the catch then returns the resolved path. A console.error here would print an error line on every successful run. The other codes already rethrow as an Error that the top-level handler prints once; logging them as well would print the message twice.

renameSync throws when another process filled the destination during the check, and has no non-throwing form. The catch already throws an Error whose message is printed once by the top-level handler (exit 2). Logging it here as well would print the message twice on stderr, and a rename error of any other code is rethrown unchanged.

This is the CLI's last handler: it prints the error message on stderr and exits 2, the code the parent contract and the tests expect for a check that could not run. Rethrowing from the top level instead gives an uncaught-error report with a stack trace and exit code 1, which the CLI reserves for a rule that broke.

The worker's exit status is its verdict to statechart.ts: 0 and 1 mean the check passed or a rule broke, and every other status becomes exit 2 with nothing written. The catch prints the message and exits 2. Rethrowing from the top level prints an uncaught-error report with a stack trace instead of the message and exits 1, which is the worker's 'a rule broke' status.
